trails.title: Data Booklet
trails.description: The handwriting on it may be strong and hasty, but it is still neat and tidy.

content.text:
※Theophil von Dittarsdorf

Member of "The Circle," deceased, relationship to the Manus Vindictae unclear. His posthumous work, The Salvation, reveals information about to the "Storm." Suspected of having had contact with members of the Manus Vindictae during his lifetime.

Hotel Sacher vs. Cafe Demel Sachertorte → Which one?

The timing can be decided  in advance.

※Gus Klint

A young man with a particular fondness for squares and diamonds. More interested in women than the Manus Vindictae.

※Egan Hilde

A Dejected? Young man. relationship to the Manus Vindictae unclear.

※Heinrich

Mentally unstable.

*Often accompanied by strange odors.

items.text: Double Cross
The scent from backstage strikes her as odd.
Something neglected within her stirs to life, pulsing in her chest—constantly pulsing, pulsing, pulsing.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Madam ... Hofmann?
Marcus stands stunned, watching her role model sink back to the ground.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Fortunately, the Guiding One has heard our cries and promised us salvation.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The "Storm" will put a stop to this frenetic melody before all the good, artistic, heartfelt things in life are destroyed before our eyes.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: It will wash away the unwanted, the unimportant. The creators of this chaos will be severely punished.
Heinrich checks his watch expectantly.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: It's still a little early for what Mr. Forget Me Not has planned. But the actors and actresses are in place.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Don't worry, Ms. Angelotti ... We won't leave anyone behind ... Nor will we leave any enemy spared.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: I will eliminate the obstacles for you, and help you better understand yourself.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What? What are you talking about?
Blood courses through her in rapid fire.
The sound grows louder and more intense until she can hear it pounding in her ears.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The "sifting" has begun, ladies.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Enjoy! The potion specially made by Mr. Forget Me Not—a gift from the Picrasma tree.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: For those who have arcanist blood, it will undoubtedly enhance their powers, both physically and mentally.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: But for the powerless mixed-blood humans ... It is lethal poison.
Watching the young arcanist stupefied by the smoke, Heinrich only chuckles.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: People sometimes forget how different humans and arcanists are, don't they? Marriages between the two races have been common for some time.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The mixed-bloods have become the majority of society. Those with less than one-fourth arcanist blood, some with even less, have blended in amongst the humans because they don't have any arcane power.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: And so, they are seen as humans both by the public and by themselves ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: And now, the punishment for betraying your own kind! You should've stood with us, but instead you sided with the enemy and watched your own kin suffer.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The blood that you have ignored and forsaken will awaken, explode, and tear you apart from within.
Marcus stubbornly supports Hofmann's arm, but Hofmann raises a hand to refuse her help.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... I'm fine ... I'm just a bit ... I can still stand.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Sadly, you won't be fine for long.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Mr. Forget Me Not is one of the best potion-makers. The formula is carefully designed to prolong your suffering until sweet death finally spreads its wings over you.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: But resent not! Your pain is fleeting compared to what my people were made to endure.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: As for you, Ms. Angelotti, a choice lies before you.
In the oddly scented smoke, Heinrich raises his hand.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: You have been lied to. Humans have whispered lies through their petty, made-up history. There has been genocide, the lengthy, vicious kind, under the banner of high-minded reason.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: They tried to split the world in two, so that the progressives cannot be stopped by the "non-progressives," so that the irrational cannot speak against the rational. When they do, death and destruction follow.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: You're one of us, an arcanist child abandoned at an orphanage. You must've heard your heart pounding like a knock on the door; it's the sound of a long-lost soul coming home.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: It calls to you to rid your shackles of reason, to expose the lies of history, to embrace your primal passions, and unleash the powers of your gift!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: You should be one of us, as you always should have been!
The aroma of the Picrasma tree comes to mind.
Yes, she hears it.
Echoes up from the reptilian brain, reverberating along tangled knots of reason and knowledge.
He's right, Marcus! This is the missing part of history that they didn't let you go through!
Hofmann kept everything from you, didn't she? She's a liar!
You're here because you want to find the truth. You don't have to work for a human institution!
The invasion of thoughts continues without end.
*thud*
A dagger is thrown to the ground, spinning on its handle.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Pick it up. Drive it into your mentor's heart. Show us your resolve.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: An opportunity has arisen. Take it. A chance to learn who you really are, where you came from, and why you were abandoned.
She picks up the dagger with blade pointing outward.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Very good, Angelotti!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Before the High One of Midnight sheds merciful tears and washes away the sins of man—pass the test and join us.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: And we will take you through the "Storm," back to our era.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Our ... era?
A tear slides across her face.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But my era has already come.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: 1914, the year you once wiped out with the "Storm," is my era!
She holds the dagger, looking up at the dome in despair.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I waited in the abandoned lighthouse of that island, I waited in the marble house of the Foundation, watching the time go back to 1966, to 1929, and finally back here ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: You say this is salvation, but you're just replacing one annihilation with another.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The Foundation wants to stop the destruction, but you are speeding it up. You don't care about this era, nor the people living in it.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: You abandon them. You hide in your empty kingdom, in-in your garden that doesn't yet exist, with your, haha, with your art, your-your poems, and your pianos, hahahaha!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And me, I just wanted to go home for a visit. Why would you take away even that?!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, don't lose control of yourself!
It's too late.
She charges toward the man.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... I'll kill you, Heinrich!!!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... Someone is calling me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Leave here with me, doctor. Let the rain wash away the old world, so we can build your dream in a new one.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I thought we were on the same side of liberating our repression, giving freedom to the arcanists.
She stretches out her hand to her.
But Kakania stands stiff, clenching and unclenching her fist in futile repetition.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I just …

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I never thought that you would take people's lives, Isolde.
Isolde looks up with a maddening joy plastered on her face.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Is this why you hesitate?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Because I killed a person who shouldn't be killed? A person from the Foundation? After you befriended the young lady?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Is it because you made peace with the Foundation, and yet I became associated with Manus Vindictae?
She found her answer. Her eyes twinkle with delight.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I see now, I understand, doctor. I will correct my mistakes.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... Isolde?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I killed a man of the Foundation, thus you thought I was imposing Manus Vindictae's cause over yours. It displeased you, am I right?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... Then I shall prove myself to you.
She produces a pistol out from beneath her skirt.
It once helped end Theophil's suffering, and now it will take on a greater mission.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I will take Heinrich's life, for that would make it fair.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Please come with me and witness my commitment, doctor.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What? What did you say? ... You're going to kill ... who?
But Isolde has already lifted her skirt, bowing gracefully to the doctor.
The familiar surge of arcane energy—the same teleportation incantation that brought Karl to the stage.
After a brief flash of light, they find themselves on the other side of the stage.
Where a fierce battle has just taken place.
Hofmann kneels in agony, tearing off her scarf to reveal the terrifying pattern of toxic veins that has spread from her heart across her chest.
The potion is indeed lethal—forcefully activating her already weak blood vessels, turning her body into an overburdened machine, ready to explode on the slightest movement.
Heinrich then did not lie—she was destined for a long, unavoidable, agonizing march toward death.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: *growls* I'm going to kill ...
And Marcus, pulled as if by fate, finds herself caught in an all-consuming emotional whirlwind from her revelations.
Her gift was not meant for battle—its misuse only makes her lose control even more.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Ms. Angelotti, if you still don't see the big picture after returning to your true self, you are not one of us.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Enjoy the "sifting" before the "Storm."
Heinrich kicks her away with indifference, no longer regarding the novice arcanist with any concern.
And at this moment, Isolde descends from the void, as if possessed by some strange deity.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Isolde, you're just in time. These two are hopeless—
The zealot's words hang in the air ...
As she smiles and raises her arm.
The deadly firearm is aimed at her once-friend, with a straight baseline and graceful arc.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... Goodbye, Heinrich.
TO BE CONTINUED…
